rules.summary: Each SII's sophistication is addressed with investor-specific facts, but several entries use templated or portfolio-listing formats without demonstrating actual expertise.

detail.explanation: Para 20 requires each SII to have the knowledge, expertise, and experience to assess the risk profile and prospects of the applicant as at the date of investment. The prospectus provides per-SII descriptions at pp.186–192. These vary materially in quality: Northern Light, Oceanpine, SummitView, Xiaomi, Tencent, and BOCGI provide substantive descriptions linking their investment focus to the relevant technology sector. However, Geely SII and SAIC Motor SII are characterised as 'key participant[s] in the downstream automotive industry' with reference to Frost & Sullivan reports — this is a market share characterisation, not a demonstration of knowledge and expertise to assess semiconductor/autonomous driving SoC risk. [R]: The Geely and SAIC characterisations do not constitute a substantiated sophistication case under para 20 without further explanation of how being a vehicle OEM equips these investors to assess the risk profile of an SoC design company.
detail.recommendation: Reviewer should consider whether Geely and SAIC's sophistication under para 21(iv) (key market participant) is adequately substantiated for para 20 purposes, given that market share data from Frost & Sullivan does not itself demonstrate expertise in assessing SoC design company risk.

rules.summary: Oceanpine and SummitView rely on para 21(iii); SummitView's disclosure is adequate but Oceanpine's AUM at the relevant reference date falls below HK$15bn and the Specialist Technology breakdown is unclear.

detail.explanation: SummitView SIIs: AUM HK$13.2bn as of December 31, 2020, 'with more than HK$5 billion in Specialist Technology Companies.' [T] re PARAM_B4_TECH_MIN: HK$5bn ✓. But [T] re PARAM_B3_PORT_MIN: total AUM HK$13.2bn < HK$15bn — this means SummitView cannot qualify under para 21(ii) (total portfolio size). It must therefore rely solely on para 21(iii), which requires AUM/portfolio 'primarily derived' from Specialist Technology investments to be at least HK$5bn. The disclosure states >HK$5bn in Specialist Technology at Dec 31, 2020 — this meets PARAM_B4_TECH_MIN. However, the Dec 31, 2020 reference date is after SummitView's investment (Series B2, September 2019); the footnote 1 convention ('not more than six months prior to definitive agreement') would place the required reference date no later than approximately March 2020. December 31, 2020 is approximately 15 months after September 2019 — this is after the definitive agreement, not before it, and therefore cannot satisfy para 25(i)/C2. This is a material reference date issue for SummitView. Oceanpine SIIs: AUM 'approximately HK$14.3 billion as of December 31, 2023 derived primarily from the valuation of their investments in Specialist Technology Companies.' [T] re PARAM_B3_PORT_MIN: HK$14.3bn < HK$15bn — cannot qualify under para 21(ii). [T] re PARAM_B4_TECH_MIN: the AUM is stated to be 'primarily derived' from Specialist Technology investments but no specific HKD figure for the Specialist Technology portion is given. At HK$14.3bn total, if 'primarily' means >50%, the Specialist Technology portion would be >HK$7.15bn ≥ PARAM_B4_TECH_MIN (HK$5bn) — but this is inferential, not stated. [D]: Oceanpine does not disclose the specific amount attributable to Specialist Technology investments.
detail.recommendation: For SummitView: reviewer should urgently check the definitive agreement date for the Series B2 investment. If signed in September 2019, the December 31, 2020 AUM reference is approximately 15 months after the agreement and does not comply with para 25(i). For Oceanpine: reviewer should obtain confirmation of the specific HKD amount of AUM attributable to Specialist Technology investments to verify PARAM_B4_TECH_MIN is met by express disclosure rather than inference.

reasoning_flags.summary: SummitView's AUM reference date (31 December 2020) appears to post-date its Series B2 investment (September 2019) by approximately 15 months, potentially violating the para 25(i) 6-month reference date rule.

detail.explanation: Tier2/pre_ipo_investment (p.189) states SummitView's AUM was HK$13.2bn 'as of 31 December 2020.' The corporate timeline in tier2/pathfinder_sii (p.176) indicates September 2019 as the date Oceanpine Capital (not SummitView) first invested; separately, the pre-IPO overview table at p.181 shows Series B2 with a first subscription date of September 25, 2019, and last payment December 2019. If SummitView's definitive agreement was signed in September–December 2019, the December 31, 2020 reference date is 12–15 months after the agreement — well beyond PARAM_C2_REF_MONTHS (6 months). Footnote 1's assertion that all figures are within 6 months prior to the definitive agreement appears inconsistent with this date gap.
detail.recommendation: Reviewer should urgently obtain the definitive agreement date for SummitView's Series B2 investment and verify whether the December 31, 2020 AUM reference date satisfies para 25(i). If the definitive agreement predates December 31, 2020 by more than 6 months, the AUM disclosure for SummitView does not comply with para 25(i) and an earlier reference date figure must be provided.

reasoning_flags.summary: Individual SII holdings sum to approximately 36.47% at LPD (post-offer basis unclear), but no single prospectus figure states total aggregate SII % for Module E compliance; post-offer percentage basis not confirmed.

detail.explanation: Summing the nine per-SII LPD figures from tier2/pre_ipo_investment gives approximately 36.47% of 'total issued shares.' However, these are pre-offer figures (LPD, before Global Offering). The prospectus does not state the post-offer aggregate SII % (on 569,169,253 post-IPO shares). The applicable threshold (15%) under para 26(ii) is applied to 'issued share capital at listing.' A pre-offer aggregate percentage on a smaller share base would overstate the post-offer percentage. The offer comprises 37,000,000 new shares (6.5% of post-offer total), meaning all existing SII percentages will be diluted by approximately 6.5% upon completion — post-offer SII aggregate would be approximately 36.47% × (1 - 0.065) ≈ 34.1%, still well above 15%. However, this calculation is not stated in the prospectus and the basis of E1 compliance is not confirmed.
detail.recommendation: Reviewer should request a single, auditable Module E compliance statement in the prospectus that: (a) states the aggregate SII % on a post-offer basis (on total issued share capital immediately after completion of the Global Offering); (b) identifies the applicable threshold (15%); and (c) confirms the benchmark is met.

reasoning_flags.summary: SII investment amounts are disclosed only in USD at the round level; no per-SII HKD investment amount is stated, making individual D3 amount threshold verification impossible from the prospectus alone.

detail.explanation: The pre-IPO overview table (p.181) states USD round totals. Individual SII descriptions state current shareholding percentages only. Para 25 requires disclosure of investment amount per SII; para 26(i)(b) requires individual Pathfinder SII investment amount of at least PARAM_D3_IND_AMT (HK$450m) as an alternative threshold. While Northern Light and Oceanpine meet the 3% threshold making the HK$450m alternative unnecessary, the absence of per-SII investment amounts in HKD means the amount limb cannot be independently verified from the prospectus for any SII. Cross-referencing tier1/cap_table does not yield per-SII investment amounts.
detail.recommendation: Reviewer should confirm whether a per-SII investment amount table exists elsewhere in the prospectus (e.g. Appendix IV). If not, the absence of per-SII investment amounts in HKD is a gap under rule C4 [D].

summary.overall_assessment: Black Sesame's Meaningful Investment disclosure structure is substantively sound — the Pathfinder SII count (2), aggregate Pathfinder holding (17.45%), individual Pathfinder holdings (11.48%/5.97%), conversion mechanics (mandatory 1:1), and lock-up obligations are all clearly disclosed and appear to meet the applicable thresholds. The principal issues are presentation and reference-date gaps rather than substantive shortfalls: no single consolidated Module E compliance statement links the aggregate SII holding to the applicable 15% threshold; the market cap tier determination is implicit rather than stated; investment amounts lack HKD conversion; and per-SII independence confirmations are templated rather than dated to the definitive agreement. The most material concerns requiring priority review are: (1) the SummitView reference date, which appears to post-date the definitive agreement by ~15 months in potential breach of para 25(i); (2) the Northern Light/Dr. Yang Lei independence reasoning gap; and (3) the absence of any express para 19 statement (no agreements to return investment) — the only Absent finding.
